detail.longDescription: I wrote a userscript in TamperMonkey to track data for the game Cheat! on neopets.com . Basically what I'm trying to do is keep track of a stack of cards, represented by an array of objects. I'm using TamperMonkey's GM.getValue and GM.setValue to save the data between sessions. This is all the code I have that affects the stack variable: Declaration: let CARDS_IN_STACK = await GM.getValue("CARDS_IN_STACK", []); Adding cards to stack (in function that finds selected cards): CARDS_IN_STACK.push(getCardByName(displayedCardsList[i].getElementsByTagName("a")[0].getElementsByTagName("img")[0].name)); When stack is picked up (cleared): CARDS_IN_STACK = []; setStorageValues(); Setting the storage value in setStorageValues() : await GM.setValue("CARDS_IN_STACK", CARDS_IN_STACK);` The problem I'm having is that after clearing the stack variable, it will sometimes load with an earlier version with the wrong value. I have no idea what could be causing this. What is causing it to work this way and is there a better way to store data that doesn't have this problem?
